Position Summary

The Finance ERP Product Manager leads business-side product management for SAP and related ERP capabilities. Reporting to the Manager, Finance Business Innovation Office (BIO), the role brings together Finance functional subject-matter experts to establish a coordinated business perspective on UHN’s SAP environment, make collective recommendations, and prioritize changes and enhancements based on business value, risk, controls, dependencies and user impact.

The role facilitates the Finance SAP user group and serves as a bridge among Finance process owners and users, BIO, Digital, Data & Analytics, project teams, vendors and implementation partners. The Product Manager is accountable for business product direction, governance, roadmap and backlog coordination, requirements facilitation, business validation and value realization. The FInance ERP Product Manager works in partnership with the Digital team, which retains accountability for technical architecture, configuration, integration engineering, deployment, production support and other technical decisions within its mandate.

In addition to ongoing SAP product management, the role contributes to assessments and implementation initiatives that integrate with SAP and may lead or support other priorities across the BIO portfolio. Assignments may evolve in response to Finance priorities, while remaining consistent with the role’s product-management, business-integration and portfolio responsibilities.

The ERP Product Manager is a proactive, collaborative leader who brings structure and direction to complex, cross-functional priorities. The successful candidate combines strategic product thinking with strong Finance business acumen and a high degree of technical curiosity. They are able to develop a strong working understanding of SAP, its configuration and data, and how it integrates with other systems and applications across the Finance landscape. They are comfortable learning how complex systems work, investigating dependencies and translating between business and technical perspectives so they can effectively challenge assumptions, assess impacts and collaborate with Digital and other technical partners. They are skilled at building consensus among stakeholders with different priorities and balancing business value, risk, urgency, controls and operational readiness. This is a unique opportunity to shape the direction of Finance ERP capabilities and improve how Finance teams use SAP to support reliable, efficient and sustainable operations at UHN.

• Establish and Facilitate the Finance SAP user group, including preparing decision materials, structuring discussions, documenting decisions and actions, and supporting transparent, collective prioritization across functional areas.
• Develop and maintain a business-led product vision, roadmap and prioritized backlog for SAP and related Finance ERP capabilities.
• Coordinate Finance process owners and functional subject-matter experts in defining business problems, requirements, business rules, controls, user needs and acceptance criteria.
• Assess enhancement requests using business value, strategic alignment, risk, urgency, control implications, user impact, dependencies, effort and operational readiness.
• Represent the Finance business perspective in discussions with Digital, Data & Analytics, vendors, system integrators and other delivery partners, while maintaining clear separation between business and technical accountabilities.

• Identify cross-process and cross-application impacts involving workflows, master data, reporting, controls, integrations and downstream operations.
• Coordinate Finance participation in solution reviews, end-to-end testing, user acceptance testing, business readiness, go-live activities and post-implementation review; operational Finance retains accountability for business acceptance.
• Monitor product and capability health, including adoption, service performance, operational risks, enhancement outcomes, lifecycle needs and opportunities for continuous improvement.

• Contribute to vendor and partner governance by reviewing proposals, estimates, assumptions, risks, deliverables and knowledge-transfer requirements from a Finance product perspective.
• Support change-management, communications, training and adoption activities in partnership with Finance Change Management, operational leaders and subject-matter experts.
• Connect SAP and ERP priorities to the broader Finance capability map, transformation roadmap and BIO portfolio, identifying dependencies, overlaps and opportunities for coordinated delivery.
• Lead or support other assessments, products, projects and portfolio priorities assigned within BIO, applying product-management, business-analysis, facilitation and governance capabilities as required.

Who We Are; What We Do; Where We’re Going

Magnet Forensics is a global leader in the development of digital investigative software that acquires, analyzes, and shares evidence from computers, smartphones, tablets, and IoT-related devices. We are continually innovating so our customers can deploy advanced and effective tools to protect their companies, communities, and countries.

Serving thousands of customers globally, our solutions are playing a crucial role in modernizing digital investigations, helping investigators fight crime, protect assets, and guard national security.

With employees based around the world, Magnet Forensics has been expanding our global presence. As a part of Magnet Forensics, you can expect to make a difference in the world, no matter what role you play. You’ll be supported through learning and development, not to mention an incredible team with unbelievable talent and integrity.

If you think you would be the right person to join our team working towards this goal, we would love to hear from you!

Role Overview

Magnet Forensics is building the next generation of its core Products, including AI-native, agentic capabilities across our digital forensics and incident response (DFIR) portfolio. This role is your opportunity to define and ship agentic experiences that change how investigators, examiners, and analysts do their most important work.

As a Lead Product Manager, you will drive the strategy and execution for driving growth, innovation and the next phase of our core Product within the Examination and Analysis space within Magnet’s product portfolio. You will work cross-functionally, partnering closely with customers, engineering, design, product marketing, data science, and go-to-market teams. You are an individual who cares of the craft of Product Management and have ran the gamut of the entire Product Lifecycle from building products 0 to 1, scaled mature products and sunset products/features. You have worked in regulated spaces in the past and believe that PM’s work with a GM mindset.

This is a high-impact individual contributor role for a builder who is energized by frontier AI, comfortable with ambiguity, and focused on adoption, growth, and outcomes that show up in the data.

What You'll Do

• Drive the product discovery of the evolution of one of Magnet’s core products: execute upon the product vision, roadmap, and success metrics for the examination and analysis product, including agentic experiences within it.

• Own the outcome like a GM: Own the success of your area end to end: strategy, roadmap, positioning inputs, pricing inputs, and the business results. Set the bar for what "good" looks like and be accountable for whether it landed, not just whether it shipped.

• Build experiences that ship: Design and deliver product that examiners and investigators actually use in casework, from core AXIOM workflows through AI-assisted capabilities (copilots, human-in-the-loop review, retrieval, automation). Production grade, reliable, and defensible.

• Build for trust and defensibility: In forensics the output has to hold up. Define verification, transparency into how a result was produced, reversibility, escalation paths, and auditability so users can defend the work downstream. Treat this as an enforced constraint, not an aspiration.

• Run continuous discovery: Engage customers and prospects through interviews, onsite visits, lab ride-alongs, workshops, and discovery sessions. Map opportunities to solutions, validate before building, and keep a living view of unmet needs.

• Decide with data: Instrument every experience, define the metrics that matter, and run a disciplined experimentation practice (A/B tests, funnels, cohort analysis) so decisions are grounded in evidence, not opinion.

• Drive adoption and growth: Own activation, onboarding, and the path to habitual use. Reduce friction, design for time to value, and build the loops that turn usage into expansion and retention. Partner with go-to-market and growth to convert capability into usage, usage into value, and value into revenue.

• Master the market: Develop deep expertise in DFIR (Digital Forensics and Incident Response), competitive dynamics, customer workflows, and where emerging technology (including AI) meaningfully changes how investigations get done. Use it to inform strategic bets.

• Navigate competing priorities: Make thoughtful tradeoffs across scope, quality, trust, and timelines while staying aligned to strategic objectives.

• Drive clarity: Break ambiguous problem spaces into structured, actionable plans that align leadership and let teams execute with confidence.

• Lead strategic visibility and alignment: Track the metrics that signal success and give clear, outcome-focused updates to executives and cross-functional partners.

• Collaborate across teams: Partner with engineering, UX, data science, and peer PMs to deliver experiences that are intuitive, consistent, and aligned to key personas.

• Influence cross-functionally: Build strong relationships with GTM, customer success, support, and leadership to drive alignment and optimize results.

• Work AI-natively: Default to AI across your own workflow (discovery, research, analysis, drafting, prototyping) and model AI-native ways of working that raise the bar for the wider product team.

• Travel: 5-15%.

• AI-native operator (required): You use AI as a default part of how you work, not an occasional assist. You are fluent with current AI tools and prompt engineering for research, discovery synthesis, competitive analysis, drafting (PRDs, specs, user stories), data analysis, and rapid prototyping.

• Experience: 7-10 years in product management, ideally with enterprise SaaS & GovTech experiences.
